description_full: Acushnet Holdings Corp. designs, develops, manufactures, and distributes golf products in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Africa, Japan, Korea, and internationally. It operates through three segments: Titleist Golf Equipment, FootJoy Golf Wear, and Golf Wear. The company offers golf equipment comprising golf clubs, such as drivers, fairways, hybrids, and iron, as well as wedges; and golf bags, headwear, and golf gloves under the Titleist, Vokey Design, and Scotty Cameron brands. It provides golf shoes, gloves, travel hear, golf outerwear, men's and women's golf apparel under the FootJoy brands; golf gear products, including golf bags, headwear, accessories; golf travel bags, luggage and other travel products under the Club Glove brand; and luxury leather golf goods under the Links & Kings brand. In addition, the company offers ski, golf, and lifestyle apparel under the KJUS brand. It sells its products through on-course golf shops and golf specialty retailers, as well as through representatives, other retailers, and online. Acushnet Holdings Corp. was formerly known as Alexandria Holdings Corp. and changed its name to Acushnet Holdings Corp. in March 2016. The company was founded in 1910 and is headquartered in Fairhaven, Massachusetts. Acushnet Holdings Corp. operates as a subsidiary of Misto Holdings Corp.

financial_summary: Acushnet Holdings Corp. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $4.7B market cap on $2.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 15% against a 8% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 52% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $120M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.03× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 5.0×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 52% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
